<description>
Enable `optin.performance.Padding` with the default of 24 bytes (made explicit in the clang-tidy config), after fixing warnings for more padding than that. Enabling it at this point would be to catch regressions above this amount.

Based on #36501, which reorders `CBlockIndex` to save 8 bytes (`clang-tidy` also warns about this). Wondering if contributors/reviewers think this is worthwhile given we may make that refactor? Also not sure if it's possible for us to enable this generally, as padding will differ depending on various factors.
</description>

[2026-11-10] c:6761452468 comment by maflcko (member):
Is this really worth it? This could make the code harder to read by having fields that belong together split further apart. See e.g. the mempool "rolling" section.

I'd say this should be an opt-in list for structs where we know they exist 1000s of times and that would benefit low-resource systems. E.g. saving 24kB on systems that have set 2000 connections (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35919), so likely they are not low-memory systems, seems a rounding error.

So my preference would be to have this opt-in per-struct and accommodate each change with a measurement, or at least a guess of how much it would save.
